new_result.statement: For any Borel F:R^n->R, the optimal interval-density constant over arbitrary independent cap-one marginals equals the optimal constant restricted to C_c^infinity marginals with one compact interval as support, positive on its interior, and pointwise strictly below one. No common support diameter or positive density floor is available.

proof_mechanism: Cap-preserving tail-mass compactification followed by convolution with a compact probability mollifier gives smooth compact cap-one L1 approximants.
Given a smooth compact cap-one density g, mix (1-epsilon)g with epsilon times a broad smooth bump q that is positive on one interval containing supp(g) and has sup(q)<1.
The mixture has one connected interval support, is positive on the interval interior, has strict cap <1, and is within 2epsilon in L1 of g.
Tensor L1 error is bounded by the sum of marginal errors and pushforward contracts total variation, so uniform interval-density constants pass with zero loss.

partner_applied.application: For Q=2X1X2+(X3+X4-beta)^2/2+ell1 X1+ell2 X2+gamma, spectrum {1,-1,1,0}, connected smooth approximants satisfy P(Q in I)<=(4+2 log 8)|I|; zero-loss TV closure gives the same bound for arbitrary fragmented/unbounded cap-one marginals.

scope_guard: Connected support is justified only as a zero-loss closure class for a uniform interval bound. No extremality, bounded interval length, uniform positive floor, derivative bounds, moments, log-concavity, or post-rotation independence are obtained.
